items.statement: Berth fees are charged per started hour from 1 May.

said.text: From May we charge berths per started hour, not per day.

items.statement: The pilot fee doubles for ships with a draught over nine metres.
Every harbour fee is shown with its tax on the invoice.
The online booking form asks for the length of the ship before the dates.
Tide tables are published a week ahead instead of a day ahead.
Tug engines get an oil change every 250 running hours.
Night shifts on the tugs last at most ten hours.

said.text: No crew shift at night longer than ten hours, agreed.

items.statement: Bunkering moves to the supplier on the north quay from June.
The weekly team call moves to Thursday mornings.
Who keeps the notes of the retrospective?
Does a booking cancelled less than a day ahead still pay the berth fee?
Divers inspect the hulls of the tugs twice a year.
The canteen gets a new coffee machine.
Crew members swap shifts through the roster only.
Fuel for the pilot boats is bought in bulk every quarter.
High water warnings go out by text message two hours ahead.
Berths can be booked ninety days in advance.
Every new colleague gets a laptop with the VPN set up.
The fleet manager approves every tug repair above 5000.
Regular callers get a discount on every harbour fee.
Spare propellers are ordered from one supplier only.
Pilot fees are billed to the agent of the ship, not to its owner.
Expense reports are due on the fifth of each month.
Should the readings of the tide gauges be kept for ten years?
Стоянка у причала оплачивается за каждый начатый час.
Планёрку перенесли на пятницу.
